def-oriented-crossing-sign-writhe-and-bl:
## Definition

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the smooth normal-bundle structure used in the
framing clause. For a knot component $K$, its normal bundle is the fibrewise
quotient $\nu K=TS^3|_K/TK$, and a normal section is a smooth section of this
bundle.

Let $D$ be a regular oriented link diagram in a projection plane $P$ of an
oriented $3$-sphere, after moving the link off the point at infinity. Fix the
unit viewing normal $n$ pointing toward the viewer. Orient $P$ by the rule that
an ordered basis $(u,v)$ of $P$ is positive exactly when $(n,u,v)$ is a positive
basis of the ambient $3$-space. At a crossing $c$, let $v_{\rm over}$ and
$v_{\rm under}$ be the nonzero projected tangent vectors following the
orientations of the overpassing and underpassing strands. Define
$$\operatorname{sgn}(c):=\operatorname{sgn}\det_P(v_{\rm over},v_{\rm under})\in\{+1,-1\}.$$
Reversing the orientation of $P$ reverses every crossing sign.

This convention makes the positive geometric Artin half twist positive. In
the braid chart $(x,y,t)$ with ambient orientation $(x,y,t)$, view along $+y$;
the induced positive orientation of the $(x,t)$ projection plane is the ordered
basis $(\partial_t,\partial_x)$. For the positive half twist, label $i$ moves
from $x=-h$ to $x=h$ below the midpoint, while label $i+1$ moves from $x=h$ to
$x=-h$ above it, with $h>0$. Thus the over and under projected tangent vectors
in coordinates $(t,x)$ are $(1,-2h)$ and $(1,2h)$, whose determinant is
$4h>0$.

The **writhe** of $D$ is
$$\operatorname{wr}(D):=\sum_{c\text{ a crossing of }D}\operatorname{sgn}(c).$$
For a link component $K_i$, its **self-writhe**
$\operatorname{wr}_i(D)$ is the sum over crossings whose two branches belong to
$K_i$; the total writhe also includes all mixed crossings between distinct
components.

The **blackboard framing** of a component of $D$ is the homotopy class of the
normal section represented by the positive quarter-turn in $P$ of the projected
oriented tangent. The projection is an immersion, so this vector never
vanishes; it is perpendicular to the projected tangent, hence also to the
spatial tangent, and therefore represents a nonzero normal section of the
component in the ambient $3$-sphere.

```tikz
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.8,>=stealth]
  \draw[->] (-1,0) -- (1,0) node[right] {$v_{\rm over}$};
  \draw[->] (0,-1) -- (0,1) node[above] {$v_{\rm under}$};
  \node[above left] at (0,0) {$+1$};
\end{tikzpicture}
```

In the displayed local chart, the over tangent is the positive horizontal
vector and the under tangent is the positive vertical vector, so the determinant
is $+1$. This figure illustrates the determinant rule only; no proof below
depends on a picture.
lem-linking-number-even-sum-and-reidemei:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $D$ be a regular oriented diagram
of a two-component oriented link in $S^3$, with components $K_1,K_2$. Write
$$S(D):=\sum_{c\text{ between }K_1\text{ and }K_2}\operatorname{sgn}(c).$$
Then $S(D)$ is even, and
$$\operatorname{lk}_D(K_1,K_2):=\frac{S(D)}2\in\mathbb Z$$
is unchanged by planar isotopy and by each oriented Reidemeister move of types
I, II, and III. Thus it has the same value on any two regular diagrams of
ambient-isotopic oriented links. It is symmetric in $K_1,K_2$; reversing exactly
one component changes its sign, and reversing both components leaves it
unchanged.
alg-oriented-linking-number-from-diagram:
## Definition

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$.

The input is a finite regular oriented link diagram together with its declared
components. If it does not have exactly two components, return
`invalid-input`. For a two-component diagram $D$, initialize $s:=0$ and make
one pass over its finite crossing list. At each crossing whose branches lie on
different components, add
$$\operatorname{sgn}\det_P(v_{\rm over},v_{\rm under})$$
to $s$, where the determinant is taken in the oriented projection plane; ignore
self-crossings. Return $s/2$. The even-sum lemma establishes that this output is
an integer and is the diagram's linking number.
thm-oriented-linking-number-scan-termina:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. On every finite regular oriented diagram
with exactly two components, the crossing-scan algorithm halts after one
iteration per crossing and returns the integer half-sum of the mixed crossing
signs. On an input with any other number of components it returns
`invalid-input` after the finite component-count check.
thm-linking-number-equals-signed-interse:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K$ and $J$ be disjoint oriented smooth
embedded circles in the oriented three-sphere, and let $\Sigma$ be a compact
oriented smooth surface embedded in the three-sphere with boundary $K$, whose
outward-normal-first boundary orientation is the specified orientation of $K$.
Here outward-normal-first means that an outward-pointing normal followed by a
positive boundary tangent gives the orientation of $\Sigma$. Assume
$J$ is transverse to $\Sigma$, and fix a regular oriented diagram $D$ of
$J\cup K$. Let $\eta$ be a positively oriented meridian of $K$ and let
$m\in\mathbb Z$ be the unique integer such that
$[J]=m[\eta]$ in $H_1(S^3\setminus K;\mathbb Z)$. Define the topological
linking number by $\operatorname{lk}(J,K):=m$. Let
$\operatorname{lk}_D(J,K)$ be the half-sum of the signs of the mixed crossings
of $D$. Orient the normal line of $\Sigma$ by the ambient orientation. A point
of $J\cap\Sigma$ has sign $+1$ if the oriented curve $J$ crosses from the
negative side of $\Sigma$ to its positive side, and sign $-1$ for the reverse
passage. Then
$$\operatorname{lk}_D(J,K)=\operatorname{lk}(J,K)=\sum_{p\in J\cap\Sigma}\operatorname{sign}_\Sigma(p).$$
The statement is conditional on a supplied spanning surface and regular
diagram; it asserts no surface- or diagram-existence theorem.
lem-framed-knot-push-off-self-linking-we:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $K:S^1\hookrightarrow S^3$ be an
oriented smooth embedded circle and let $s$ be a smooth nowhere-zero section of
its normal bundle. For any tubular neighbourhood chart that is the inclusion
on the zero section and identifies each vertical normal fibre with the ambient
normal quotient by the identity, the curve $K_{\varepsilon s}$ obtained by
mapping the graph of $\varepsilon s$ into $S^3$ is an embedded oriented circle
disjoint from $K$ for every sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$. The integer
linking number of $K$ with $K_{\varepsilon s}$ is independent of the sufficiently
small radius, of the representative section in its homotopy class, and of the
normalized tubular chart. It therefore defines a self-linking integer of the
framing class $[s]$.
def-framed-knot-self-linking-and-seifert:
## Definition

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For an oriented smooth knot
$K:S^1\hookrightarrow S^3$, its normal bundle is
$\nu K=TS^3|_K/TK$, oriented so that a positive tangent to $K$ followed by a
positive basis of a normal fibre gives the ambient orientation. A **framing**
of $K$ is a homotopy class through smooth nowhere-zero sections of $\nu K$.
The normal bundle is made a smooth vector bundle under this axiom; a framed
knot includes the section class as data, not a choice made afterwards. For the
relative integer use the round metric transferred from the unit sphere in
$\mathbb R^4$ by the explicit diffeomorphism
$$x\longmapsto\left(\frac{2x}{1+\lVert x\rVert^2},\frac{\lVert x\rVert^2-1}{1+\lVert x\rVert^2}\right),\qquad\infty\longmapsto(0,0,0,1).$$
It induces a smooth bundle metric on $\nu K$. The resulting winding number is
independent of the metric: any two smooth fibre metrics interpolate through
positive metrics and the corresponding angle maps are homotopic.

Given a reference framing $[s_0]$ and another framing $[s_1]$, use a bundle
metric and the positive quarter-turn $J$ on each oriented normal plane to write
the normalized representative of $s_1$ as
$$s_1(x)=\cos\theta(x)s_0(x)+\sin\theta(x)Js_0(x).$$
The resulting map $S^1\to S^1$ has a continuous angle lift along a parameter
interval $[0,1]$: subdivide into finitely many intervals whose images lie in
open semicircles and choose consecutive local arguments agreeing at endpoints.
Since the map is closed, the lift changes by $2\pi m$ for some $m\in\mathbb Z$;
different lifts differ by a constant multiple of $2\pi$, and homotopies keep
$m$ fixed. This integer $m$ is the **relative framing integer** of $[s_1]$
with respect to $[s_0]$. Thus, once a reference framing is supplied, the
framing classes are an integer torsor; no absolute integer is assigned before
choosing a reference.

The **self-linking number** of a framed knot $(K,[s])$ is the linking number
of $K$ with a sufficiently small push-off along $s$, oriented parallel to $K$.
The push-off and its integer are independent of the representative section,
small radius, and normalized tubular chart by the preceding well-definedness
result.

If a compact oriented surface $\Sigma$ is supplied with boundary $K$, its
**Seifert framing relative to $\Sigma$** is the homotopy class of the inward
unit conormal to $K$ in $\Sigma$, viewed as a nonzero normal section to $K$ in
$S^3$. This definition is relative to the supplied surface; it neither asserts
that every knot bounds such a surface nor asserts the self-linking-zero result.
thm-blackboard-framing-self-linking-is-w:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $D$ be a regular oriented diagram
of a knot $K$ with blackboard framing $b_D$. The self-linking number of the
framed knot $(K,b_D)$ equals the diagram writhe:
$$\operatorname{sl}(K,b_D)=\operatorname{wr}(D).$$
For a link component $K_i$, the corresponding self-linking number is its
self-writhe $\operatorname{wr}_i(D)$. Total writhe of a link still includes
the signs of mixed crossings, while the sum of component self-linking numbers
uses only self-crossings.
thm-linking-number-is-invariant-and-writ:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For any two regular oriented diagrams
of ambient-isotopic two-component links, the algorithmic linking numbers
agree. Creating a positive type-I kink increases total writhe by $1$ and
deleting it decreases writhe by $1$; creating a negative kink decreases writhe
by $1$ and deleting it increases writhe by $1$. Types II and III leave total
writhe unchanged. For a knot
component, blackboard self-linking changes by the same amount under a type-I
move. Consequently writhe and blackboard self-linking are not invariants of
unframed ambient isotopy, although the integer linking number of two distinct
components is.
